title: Pinning Watchtower: Auto-eval Sequencer for Catalog & Tenant Version Upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:

We need a lightweight, reliable mechanism that automatically schedules targeted quality checks (e.g., smoke/eval runs) whenever a model version is pinned or upgraded — whether that change originates from the central catalog or a tenant-level pin. Existing approaches are ad-hoc: some upgrades trigger full pipelines (costly) while others rely on manual QA. The Pinning Watchtower is a coordinator service + policy layer that decides when, what, and how to run evaluations for pin/upgrade events.

Goals:
- Ensure upgrades (catalog -> tenant, tenant-pinned upgrades) surface regressions quickly without incurring unnecessary compute cost.
- Provide deterministic priority and sampling rules so high-risk tenants and catalog promotions get broader eval coverage.
- Integrate with the eval orchestrator and the runtime to allow fast smoke checks (latency, top-k diffs, hallucination heuristics).
- Provide observability (kickoff events, run outcomes, cost estimates) surfaced in Console and incident channels.

Scope (this ticket):
- Design and implement the Pinning Watchtower policy engine and a sequencer that emits eval jobs to the eval-orch.
- Define per-tenant and catalog-level default policies; expose simple config options for product/CS teams.
- Sampling strategy implementation: deterministic hashing + tenant priority overrides.
- Cost guard: budget cap per tenant and backoff when eval budget is exhausted.
- Minimal Console UI hooks (status indicator + last-eval result) — integration work tracked in a follow-up ticket.

Out of scope (this ticket):
- Full UI for configuring complex policies per tenant (follow-up).
- Large-scale rework of eval-orch internals. We will use the existing eval-orch API surface (ENG-53109) and augment inputs.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Event ingestion: Watchtower subscribes to pin-change events from catalog service and tenant config service. Events include source (catalog/tenant), model id, old_version, new_version, triggering_user, and tenant_id (when applicable).
2) Risk scoring: lightweight deterministic risk score computed from: source (catalog=high, tenant=medium), traffic share (high-traffic tenants increase score), whether the new version is a different quantization or architecture, and if the version is marked experimental.
3) Sampling & priority: policy evaluates score against tenant and global sampling rate. Deterministic sampling uses tenant_id hash to ensure repeatability. Higher priority => broader test suites.
4) Job emission: create a job descriptor with test-suite profile (smoke | behavioral-smoke | regression-sample), timeout, and required budget estimate. Submit to eval-orch via documented API, include 'watchtower_metadata' so runs are traceable.
5) Cost guard/backoff: if estimated cost exceeds tenant budget or global eval budget for the cycle, downgrade to smaller test-suite or schedule a deferred run, and emit an alert.
6) Observability: emit structured events (kickoff, accepted, throttled, finished, failed) to Console and to the internal events pipeline.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full-run vs sampled runs: full evaluations provide confidence but are expensive. We choose a mixed strategy: prioritized full runs for catalog promotions + high-risk tenants, sampled/short suites for low-risk tenant pins.
- Deterministic sampling vs purely random: deterministic avoids flapping sampling behavior across repeated upgrade attempts for the same tenant.
- Immediate vs deferred runs: defer low-priority runs to low-cost windows (off-peak) to reduce interference with production and cost.

Acceptance criteria (definition of done):
acceptance_criteria: Watchtower subscribes to pin-change events and logs incoming events to internal audit topic
Risk scoring and sampling decision implemented and configurable via feature flags
Watchtower emits properly formatted eval job descriptors accepted by eval-orch (ENG-53109)
Cost guard enforces tenant-level and global budget limits and downgrades jobs when needed
Kickoff/finish/throttle events are visible in the events stream and mapped to console indicators
Integration demo run showing a catalog promotion triggers a prioritized full smoke and a tenant pin triggers a sampled quick-suite
notes: We must ensure watchtower metadata includes model_version, pin_origin, and correlation_id for traceability
Coordinate with Runtime team on fast smoke hooks for latency/regression probes (ENG-77192 is related)
Budget accounting should reuse the existing billing estimates from the eval-orch to avoid duplication
Feature flag gating required to roll out: 'watchtower_enabled' and 'watchtower_cost_guard'

2025-04-01 - Maya Alvarez (QA): Proposed a short behavioral-smoke suite that runs 8 canonical prompts across customer personas. Suggested adding a 'semantic-delta' metric to compare output embeddings.
2025-04-03 - Security Review: Confirmed no new secrets or key access required. Watchtower will only reference tenant_id and model metadata. Marking security_review_required=false for now.

2025-04-04 - Liam Chen: Implemented sampling engine prototype and local simulation shows expected 2.3% of low-risk tenant pins get sampled under default policy. Pushing for integration test with eval-orch next.
